insights: The abstract Galois power frob^d is the concrete map x->x^(p^d) (frob_pow_apply); this bridge turns every fixed-field statement into a statement about solutions of x^(p^d)=x.

The degree drop is not constructed but forced: Artin gives [K:fixedField]=#<frob^d>=n/d, the tower law cancels n/d to leave [fixedField:F_p]=d. The subfield size is a consequence of the subgroup index.
Restricting to divisors d|n is essential: for a non-divisor, <frob^d> has order n/gcd(n,d) and fixes F_{p^gcd(n,d)}; only d|n makes orderOf(frob^d)=n/d and the degree come out to d.
Injectivity of d->fixedField<frob^d> is a pure cardinality argument: distinct counts p^d (p>=2) imply distinct subfields - the forward half of the subfield<->divisor bijection.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has the general Galois pieces (finrank_fixedField_eq_card, finrank_mul_finrank, card_eq_pow_finrank) but not the assembled finite-field divisor-lattice count fixedField<frob^d>=F_{p^d} / #{x:x^(p^d)=x}=p^d - this entry supplies that assembly.
nextSteps: Prove the surjective half: every intermediate field F_p <= L <= K equals fixedField<frob^d> for d=[L:F_p], upgrading InjOn to a genuine bijection {subfields of F_{p^n}}~={divisors of n}.
Recover the lattice (not just set) isomorphism: F_{p^d}<=F_{p^e} <-> <frob^e> <= <frob^d> <-> d|e.
